title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task) we enforced shared-initial generation semantics so each pair compares the identical initial candidate (baseline) to the final guarded artifact (after deterministic validation and at most one automated repair). Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The pre-registered large-effect confirmatory hypothesis (sized for large absolute changes) is not supported because the observed baseline-error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed. We add two reviewer-requested forensic items inline: (1) the observed per-vendor outcome table (baseline and guarded successes/failures by planned stratum) and (2) the identifier and archive pointer for the single discordant episode that the validator+repair corrected. All primary artifacts, per-episode validator traces, and SHA-256 digests are archived and explicitly referenced for deterministic audit.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs can translate operator intent into device-specific network configurations, promising reduced operator effort for routine NetOps changes. Incorrect or out-of-order commands can cause outages or violate workflow policies; production proposals therefore commonly interpose deterministic validators and automated repair loops as guardrails in generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines. Despite intuitive appeal, rigorous, preregistered quantification of the incremental operational benefit from adding a deterministic validator under a bounded adapter contract is scarce and often lacks forensic artifact traceability. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our principal contributions are (i) a preregistered paired estimand and confirmatory analysis with explicit missingness and retry rules, (ii) a forensic execution manifest with per-episode validator_trace objects and cryptographic digests for deterministic auditing, and (iii) a compact empirical run (N=200 pairs) that illustrates how low baseline error prevalence constrains confirmatory inference for large absolute-effect hypotheses.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification methods and runtime validators are foundational tools for preventing misconfiguration-induced outages. The canonical static-check approach is Header Space Analysis (Kazemian, Varghese, and McKeown, "Header Space Analysis: static checking for networks", 2012; see http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/summary?doi=10.1.1.228.5064), and incremental/online checkers (e.g., VeriFlow [Khurshid et al., SIGCOMM 2013, DOI:10.1145/2342441.2342452]) extend these ideas for staged updates. Recent LLM→NetOps evaluations (e.g., NetConfEval [Wang et al., DOI:10.1145/3656296], Lira et al., 2024) examine generator accuracy, sequencing and policy violations, and repair loops; surveys (Long et al., 2025; others 2024–2025) report a frequent absence of deterministic validator traces and cryptographic artifact manifests required for forensic reproducibility. Our work situates itself at that intersection and emphasizes preregistration plus artifact-first forensic bindings to support deterministic audits of paired estimator contingency cells.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration summary. We preregistered a paired binary design with N=200 intent→configuration tasks stratified by vendor family (planned strata: Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67). The primary_estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = non-actionable configuration). The confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two-sided test; a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) was prespecified. See preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a308... for full specification.

Adapter and execution contract. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e2...). The adapter enforced shared_initial_generation semantics (single initial candidate reused by both baseline and guarded conditions) and permitted at most one automated repair call per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Execution summary: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair) (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). Provider-call accounting and stage counts are archived in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...).

Synthetic task bank, validator, and scoring. The task bank was generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, workflow policies, allowed touched fields, and an explicit required_sequence. The deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parses outputs into canonical ASTs, verifies vendor syntax, enforces intent-constraints and dependency sequencing, and runs simulator-backed semantic assertions. The validator emits per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before/after) and a binary score via scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Per-episode scoring JSONs and their SHA-256 digests are archived under execution/scoring/ (see Disclosure).

Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729).

The per-episode validator_trace for pair-000137 records repair_applied = true and includes validation_before/after normalized_configurations for transparent inspection.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained execution (synthetic 200-task bank; gpt-5-mini; deterministic_netops_validator_v5; single repair attempt), the guarded pipeline corrected the sole observed actionable misconfiguration (the Juniper-like stratum pair-000137) reducing failures from 1→0. Because baseline failures were exceptionally rare (1/200), the absolute room for improvement was small and the preregistered power calibration (targeted at large absolute effects) is not informative for the observed rare-failure regime. The contingency counts and bootstrap CI are consistent and fully archived for auditing; provider_call_audit shows the adapter invoked automated repair exactly once (stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 200, repair = 1; deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...).

Implications. Marginal utility of deterministic validators depends on baseline-generator error prevalence, validator semantic coverage, repair budget, and the operational cost of an undetected actionable error. When baseline failure prevalence is very low, heavy validator investment yields small average improvements but may still prevent occasional costly outages. Experimental designs targeting rare catastrophic risks should consider cost-weighted estimands or oversampling high-difficulty strata to increase discordant mass and statistical sensitivity.

Limitations and follow-ups. Single-model evidence (gpt-5-mini); synthetic benchmark shape and validator scope limit external validity; single repair attempt enforced by adapter contract; observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) limited confirmatory power for large absolute-effect hypotheses. We preserved all per-episode validator_trace objects and cryptographic digests so auditors can (i) recompute per-stratum aggregates, (ii) inspect the discordant episode (pair-000137), and (iii) cluster residual violation codes in runs with more residual errors.
sections.conclusion: We ran a preregistered paired experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard in an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a conservative adapter contract. On the synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered confirmatory large-effect claim (sized for large absolute reductions) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence was far smaller than assumed; nevertheless, the run demonstrates that a guarded GVR loop can correct rare actionable mistakes and that complete forensic artifact traces (per-episode validator_traces and SHA-256 digests) enable deterministic audit and exact reconstruction of contingency cells. Future work should broaden model diversity, increase task realism and N, explore larger repair budgets, and evaluate cost-weighted estimands tuned to rare catastrophic failure regimes.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Requested per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are now printed inline above and are deterministically reproducible from the archived artifacts referenced by SHA-256 digests in this Disclosure.
